name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,492

clue.text: Uproar! Met foe, ice broken - so 11 said

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A noisy scene where someone met an enemy and the ice was broken, reported as a quotation from 11.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is CHAMBERLAIN: Neville Chamberlain announced 'peace for our time' on returning from Munich in 1938.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the famous claim made by Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain after signing the 1938 agreement with Hitler.

clue.text: Area noble rules, proper, accepting respectable party I overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so the letter I is dropped from the word for respectable
a word accepting others takes them in, so the word for proper wraps around what follows

blocks.note: prim means proper and correct in manner
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A noble's realm described as proper and hosting a respectable party, with the speaker left off the guest list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area noble rules' is the definition as a whole: the territory a noble rules over.
explanation.definitionFit: A princedom is the territory over which a prince, a nobleman, holds sovereign power.

clue.text: A very quiet listener, silent initially, comes into view

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word silent only

blocks.note: pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A hushed eavesdropper, saying nothing, steps out where they can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to become visible, so the verb in third person matches emerging into sight.

clue.text: Not entirely impartial girl

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for impartial is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Describing a girl who is not completely fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is a girl's name, used in crosswords for any girl or woman.

clue.text: One watching outside broadcast with restaurant worker

blocks.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for outside broadcast

explanation.surface: Someone watching a TV crew's outside broadcast alongside a waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is a person who watches or notices events without taking part.

clue.text: Last of home gatherings

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: Talking about the final house party of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of' looks like a request for a final letter, but Last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last of anything.

clue.text: Referring to game at Twickenham, nation’s latest, that’s shown again

indicators.note: the latest of something is its most recent, here the end letter of nation

blocks.note: re means concerning or referring to
Twickenham is England's rugby stadium; RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A report on an England rugby match being repeated on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a programme broadcast once more, a repeat screening.

clue.text: Put into office wearing seconds? Hard to believe!

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for seconds
as in a tall story, one hard to believe

explanation.surface: Amazement that someone could be sworn into a post while dressed in cheap rejects.
explanation.walkthrough: Seconds looks like the flawed goods someone might wear, but it is just the unit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to place them formally in an official position.

clue.text: Precise court overturning dismissal at first

indicators.note: overturning turns something upside down, so in a down entry the word for dismissal reads backwards
at first places the turned word before the abbreviation for court

blocks.note: getting the axe means being sacked
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A court reversing a worker's sacking, described as precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means accurate in every detail, a direct synonym of precise.

clue.text: I work for Independent, say, in Shanghai?

blocks.note: a staffer would say I'm with them, I am
the Independent is a newspaper, an example of the press

explanation.surface: A journalist on the Independent wondering about a posting in the Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a reporter's boast, I'm press. Shanghai is not the city but the verb meaning to force someone to serve on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress and to shanghai both mean to force men into naval or ship service against their will.

clue.text: Large place is useful at first, area for redevelopment

indicators.note: at first keeps only the opening letter of useful
a site for redevelopment is torn down and rebuilt in a new layout

explanation.surface: A planner's note that a big site would be handy to rebuild.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia, the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, is certainly a large place on the map.

clue.text: Hall, city home for leader

blocks.note: a chamber is a large hall or meeting room

explanation.surface: A town hall in a city serving as the residence of a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's theme is Neville Chamberlain, British Prime Minister at the time of the 1938 Munich Agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Neville Chamberlain led Britain as Prime Minister from 1937 to 1940.

clue.text: Simple article is written up - set in ancient times

indicators.note: written up in a down entry means written from the bottom, so the small word is read backwards
set in places these letters inside the abbreviation for ancient times

explanation.surface: A plain essay about something from antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means elementary or plain, with no extras, just like simple.

clue.text: Cunning, finding time to supplant king in vessel

indicators.note: to supplant is to take the place of, so one letter swaps out another

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A sly plotter seizing the moment to replace the monarch aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean craft or guile, as in 'arts and wiles', so it serves for cunning.

clue.text: Sir’s date worked out badly?

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are reworked and arranged anew

explanation.surface: A knight's romantic evening that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a date that went badly is a disaster, and the letters of Sir's date rearrange to say so.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is something that turns out very badly, a calamity or fiasco.

clue.text: Leader’s girl’s accommodating Italian learner

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the girl's word houses the others

blocks.note: It is short for Italian, as in gin and It
L for learner, as on learner plates

explanation.surface: A leader's daughter putting up an Italian student.
explanation.walkthrough: Adolf Hitler, the German leader with whom Chamberlain negotiated at Munich.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitler was the Führer, literally 'leader', of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: French department’s unusual soiree, nothing missed out

indicators.note: missed out means omitted, so the letter for nothing is removed
something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters are not in their normal order

explanation.surface: A French government ministry throwing an odd evening party with nothing left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Isère is a département in south-eastern France, around Grenoble.

clue.text: After climbing a hill, board can be brought around

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means going upwards, so these letters read from the bottom
after places the word for board behind the turned piece

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
board as in table: board and lodging

explanation.surface: A walker reaching a summit and finding a signboard that swivels.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotatable can be turned round on an axis, so it can be brought around.

clue.text: Forbidden, a French novel ultimately unpleasant

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of novel counts

explanation.surface: A banned French book whose ending is nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel ultimately' looks like anagram signalling, but novel is just the word that gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlawful means not permitted by law, i.e. forbidden.

clue.text: Champ embracing one in conference centre

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the word for champ wraps around the numeral

blocks.note: to champ is to chew noisily, to munch

explanation.surface: A sports champion hugging a fellow delegate at a summit venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Champ looks like a winner, but it is the verb for chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich hosted the 1938 conference where Chamberlain, Hitler and others signed the Munich Agreement.

clue.text: Tart brought up tho crushed inside? Indeed!

indicators.note: brought up in a down entry means raised from the bottom, so the word for tart reads upwards
something crushed is mangled out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
inside puts the mangled small word within the turned word for tart

blocks.note: a flan is an open tart

explanation.surface: Surprise that a pastry served up was squashed in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for emphatic agreement, meaning 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'not half!' is an emphatic British yes, meaning very much so, like indeed.

clue.text: Spinning stroke from bounder, cute

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters come straight out of the next words

explanation.surface: A charming cad playing a tricky spinning shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A bounder is an old British word for a dishonourable man, a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis or golf an undercut is a stroke that imparts backspin to the ball.

clue.text: He meets rising anger in firm for so long

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means going upward, so the word for anger is read from the bottom
in places these letters inside the abbreviation for firm
meets puts the pronoun directly beside the turned word for anger

explanation.surface: A man getting increasingly angry in his company for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For so long' reads as a duration, but 'so long' is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio and so long are both informal ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Part of match fixed by agreement

blocks.note: first meaning: a division of a tennis match
second meaning: settled or arranged in advance

explanation.surface: Hints of a match-fixing scandal in which part of the game was rigged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis match is played in sets, and a price or date that is set has been fixed by agreement.

clue.text: Chaos upset United supporters

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down entry the word for supporters is turned upside down

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: Mayhem as Manchester United's followers are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Snafu is originally US military slang for a chaotic foul-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a state of confusion or a muddle, so it serves as chaos.

clue.text: Suitable to include vegetables provided by English chaps - 11’s policy

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the word for suitable surrounds the rest
provided by simply adds the following pieces on after the vegetables

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A recipe of vegetables served by Englishmen, oddly called a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlain's policy toward Nazi Germany was appeasement, conceding demands to avoid war.

clue.text: A part of nun’s clothing, we hear, to be of use

indicators.note: we hear means the words are to be judged by how they are spoken

blocks.note: a veil is part of a nun's habit

explanation.surface: Remarks about a nun's headwear proving handy.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of help or advantage, as in 'it will avail you nothing'.

clue.text: Boys painted place, it’s looking up

indicators.note: looking up in a down entry means facing upward, so the little word is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Boys have redecorated a room, and things are improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boys painted' reads as lads doing decorating, but it means boys depicted in paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the chubby naked infant boys, cherubs, shown in Renaissance and Baroque paintings.

clue.text: A mother encounters worker, unyielding

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A mother meets a labourer who will not budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means refusing to be persuaded or to change one's mind, firmly resolute.

clue.text: Joke after warning needed for cut of beef

indicators.note: after places the word for joke behind the warning cry

blocks.note: golfers shout fore as a warning
to rib is to tease or joke

explanation.surface: A prank pulled after a warning, oddly required for a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Forerib is a joint of beef taken from the front ribs, a classic roasting cut.

clue.text: Radical friend regularly visited

indicators.note: regularly visited means calling at every other stop, so alternate letters of friend are kept

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of friend

explanation.surface: A left-wing friend who often dropped round.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a common label for a political radical, especially a communist or socialist.

clue.text: Uphill feel found unfortunately - fate of 1 Across

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters end up in a mess

explanation.surface: A climber finding the going tough, a sad end to some earlier wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Across is PEACE FOR OUR TIME; war broke out within a year of Munich.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlain's promise was dashed when war came in 1939, so it became a hope never realised.
